system_description.narrative_title: Multipolar disorder: wars, AI upheaval and economic stress
system_description.narrative_summary: The global order is an open, tightly coupled system under stress from simultaneous kinetic conflicts (Ukraine, Iran/Israel-region), deep transformations in technology and markets driven by AI, and a fragile macro-financial environment as central banks wrestle with inflation. Energy and commodity shocks from the wars amplify political fractures, while elections, migration and elite realignments increase volatility and policy unpredictability. These interacting processes create feedbacks that can rapidly amplify local shocks into systemic disturbances across finance, supply chains and alliance politics.
system_description.scope: Nation-states and alliances; ongoing armed conflicts and diplomatic mediation; global energy, commodity and financial markets; central banks and monetary policy; major technology firms, AI development and regulation; elections, political movements and migration flows; supply chains and corporate strategies.
system_description.super_system: The integrated international political-economic-security-technology system (the global order)
adjacent_subsystems: Regional security complexes (Middle East, Europe-Ukraine-Russia, East Asia-Taiwan)
Global financial and monetary system (central banks, bond and credit markets)
Global technology and AI innovation ecosystem (Big Tech, chipmakers, startups, regulators)
Energy and commodity markets (oil, gas, refining, storage, mining)

variables.name: Russia–Ukraine war
variables.description: Russia's offensive and Ukraine's defence, backed by Western military and economic support, continue to produce shifting frontlines, strikes and diplomatic pressures that reshape European security and defence burdens.

variables.name: Iran–Gulf/Middle East standoff
variables.description: Iran, Israel, the United States and Gulf states are engaged in an escalating cycle of maritime attacks, proxy strikes and diplomatic manoeuvres that raise the risk of wider regional conflict and threaten energy transit routes.

variables.name: US–China tech and trade rivalry
variables.description: The United States and China are contesting leadership in semiconductors, AI and critical supply chains through export controls, investment screening and industrial policy, reshaping global technology ecosystems and commercial linkages.

variables.name: AI-driven economic and market shift
variables.description: Rapid corporate AI deployment and heavy investor capital flows are reallocating labour, industrial demand and corporate strategy across advanced economies, creating market volatility, corporate restructuring and new sources of economic power.

variables.name: European political and fiscal cohesion crisis
variables.description: EU member states and institutions are confronting political fragmentation, debt and inflation pressures, and divergent approaches to defence and energy policy that strain collective decision‑making and burden‑sharing within Europe.
